original_question: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q pseudo algebraically closed, meaning that every absolutely irreducible Q-variety has a Qsolv-rational point? Equivalently, does every absolutely irreducible Q-variety admit a solvable rational point?
target_in_paper: Section 6, "Radically closed fields," specifically the Q_solv instance of the paper’s unnumbered open problem: whether the maximal solvable extension Q_solv of Q is ample; this appears in the broader context of asking whether radically closed fields are ample. ([smf.emath.fr](https://smf.emath.fr/sites/default/files/2020-04/smf_sec_27_montage__sample.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: It correctly singles out the field Q_solv and the general theme of a universal rational-point property over that field. ([tau.ac.il](https://www.tau.ac.il/~haran/Papers/theta-hilbertian.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s target property is ampleness, not pseudo-algebraic closedness (PAC); PAC is stronger and is not the paper’s formulation here. ([tau.ac.il](https://www.tau.ac.il/~haran/Papers/theta-hilbertian.pdf))

The paper formulates the question for smooth curves over Q_solv, not for arbitrary absolutely irreducible Q-varieties. ([liorbarysoroker.wordpress.com](https://liorbarysoroker.wordpress.com/category/hilbertian-fields/))

The ambient field in the question is Q_solv itself; the paper does not formulate the problem as existence of a solvable point on every Q-variety. ([tau.ac.il](https://www.tau.ac.il/~haran/Papers/theta-hilbertian.pdf))

To be stand-alone, Q_solv should be identified as the maximal solvable (equivalently prosolvable) extension of Q inside a fixed algebraic closure. ([tau.ac.il](https://www.tau.ac.il/~haran/Papers/theta-hilbertian.pdf))

If one uses the equivalent curve-theoretic form of ampleness, one must say either: every smooth Q_solv-curve with one Q_solv-point has infinitely many Q_solv-points, or equivalently every smooth Q_solv-curve has either 0 or infinitely many Q_solv-points. ([liorbarysoroker.wordpress.com](https://liorbarysoroker.wordpress.com/category/hilbertian-fields/))
refined_question: Let Q_solv be the maximal solvable extension of Q inside a fixed algebraic closure of Q. Is Q_solv an ample field; that is, does every smooth curve over Q_solv that has a Q_solv-rational point necessarily have infinitely many Q_solv-rational points? ([tau.ac.il](https://www.tau.ac.il/~haran/Papers/theta-hilbertian.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does every smooth curve over Q_solv have either no Q_solv-rational points or infinitely many Q_solv-rational points? ([liorbarysoroker.wordpress.com](https://liorbarysoroker.wordpress.com/category/hilbertian-fields/))
justification: Your draft is close only in the choice of the example field Q_solv and in its rational-point flavor. The paper’s actual nearby problem is not the PAC question for absolutely irreducible varieties; rather, in Section 6 it asks about ampleness, with Q_solv arising as the key motivating example among radically closed fields. So the faithful repair is to replace PAC by ample and to replace arbitrary absolutely irreducible varieties over Q by smooth curves over Q_solv. ([smf.emath.fr](https://smf.emath.fr/sites/default/files/2020-04/smf_sec_27_montage__sample.pdf?utm_source=openai))

citations.label: Radically closed fields; unnumbered open problem concerning Q_solv as a motivating instance
